sentences.zh: 但就像斯特凡·莫利纽克斯和加文·麦金尼斯一样，他的视频被取消了变现资格。

sentences.zh: 就像是，他们再也无法从YouTube视频中赚取任何广告费了。

sentences.en: Yeah, meaning it's gotten a lot harder for some of them to make a full-time living making YouTube videos.
sentences.zh: 对，这意味着他们中的一些人要靠制作YouTube视频谋生变得更加困难了。

sentences.zh: 我们现在在加利福尼亚州圣布鲁诺。

sentences.zh: 在旧金山南部不远的地方。

sentences.en: And the two of us drove down to YouTube's headquarters.
sentences.zh: 我们俩开车来到了YouTube总部。

sentences.en: That building that looks like an insurance company or something...
sentences.zh: 那个看起来像保险公司或者什么的建筑……

sentences.zh: 那就是YouTube。

sentences.en: And why are we here?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么会在这里？

sentences.en: And we went there to talk to YouTube's CEO, Susan Wojcicki.
sentences.zh: 我们去那里是为了采访YouTube的首席执行官苏珊·沃西基。

sentences.en: She's someone who has seen kind of the entire evolution of the modern internet.
sentences.zh: 她可以说是见证了整个现代互联网演变的人。

sentences.en: She's got the steering wheel of this giant, powerful, artificial intelligence that runs YouTube.
sentences.zh: 她掌握着运行YouTube这个庞大而强大的人工智能的方向盘。

sentences.zh: 我们是来采访的。

sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.zh: 真是不好意思。

sentences.en: No worries.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: And anything that she does with that power, it has all these downstream consequences.
sentences.zh: 她用这种权力所做的任何事情，都会产生所有这些下游影响。

sentences.en: So a couple years ago, I guess now, they had a shooting here.
sentences.zh: 所以我想大概几年前，他们这里发生了一起枪击事件。

sentences.en: A person who was a YouTube creator who was upset about her channel and ad money and things
sentences.zh: 有一个人是YouTube创作者，对她的频道、广告收入和诸如此类的事情感到不满，

sentences.en: like that, she actually came onto this campus with a gun and shot three people and shot herself.
sentences.zh: 她居然带着枪闯入了这个园区，枪击了三个人，然后自杀了。

sentences.en: It was a really horrible, traumatic thing for the people here.
sentences.zh: 对这里的人来说，这是一件非常可怕、创伤极大的事情。

sentences.en: And so as a result, they've really stepped up security.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们真正加强了安保。

sentences.en: So I'm not surprised that we're getting scoped out by the security guys.
sentences.zh: 所以我对安保人员盯着我们并不感到惊讶。

sentences.en: We'll go this way.
sentences.zh: 我们走这边。

sentences.en: You guys can follow me.
sentences.zh: 你们可以跟我来。

sentences.en: So they lead us inside.
sentences.zh: 于是他们把我们带了进去。

sentences.en: So this is the lobby.
sentences.zh: 这里是大厅。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is the lobby.
sentences.zh: 对，这里是大厅。

sentences.en: And we go down this set of back stairs.
sentences.zh: 我们顺着这组后楼梯走下去。

sentences.en: I've been here, but not to the basement.
sentences.zh: 我来过这里，但没去过地下室。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: Is this just studios down here?
sentences.zh: 下面全都是工作室吗？

sentences.en: And that's where we meet.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就在那里见到了她。

sentences.en: Hey, how are you?
sentences.zh: 嘿，你好吗？

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你呢？

sentences.en: Susan.
sentences.zh: 苏珊。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Julia.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是朱莉娅。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: Nice to meet you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Nice to meet you, too.
sentences.zh: 我也很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Before we get into the interview itself, like, what is Susan like as a person?
sentences.zh: 在我们进入采访本身之前，苏珊是一个什么样的人？

sentences.en: Like, what was your first impression of her?
sentences.zh: 比如，你对她的第一印象是什么？

sentences.en: Hey, let's grab you a chair.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我们给你拿把椅子。

sentences.en: So how are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: Doing okay.
sentences.zh: 还行。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你呢？

sentences.en: She doesn't really have, like, tech CEO vibes.
sentences.zh: 她身上其实没有那种科技公司CEO的气质。

sentences.en: I did not major in computer science.
sentences.zh: 我大学主修的不是计算机科学。

sentences.en: I have a history and literature undergraduate degree.
sentences.zh: 我拥有历史和文学本科学位。

sentences.en: She doesn't really get the same kind of attention as Mark Zuckerberg or Jack Dorsey.
sentences.zh: 她没有受到像马克·扎克伯格或杰克·多西那样多的关注。

sentences.en: What was an early memory for you of the internet and what you thought it was?
sentences.zh: 你对互联网的早期记忆是什么，你当时觉得它是什么？

sentences.en: Well, I first saw the internet probably in my late 20s.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我第一次看到互联网大概是在我快30岁的时候。

sentences.en: But she's actually been around the tech world for longer than either of them.
sentences.zh: 但她其实在科技界的时间比他们俩都要长。

sentences.en: And of course, I remember Netscape.
sentences.zh: 当然，我还记得网景。

sentences.en: Like, Google actually started in her garage.
sentences.zh: 就像，谷歌其实是在她的车库里创立的。

sentences.en: What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 这是什么意思？

sentences.en: It's sort of a wild piece of Silicon Valley trivia.
sentences.zh: 这算是硅谷的一段疯狂趣闻。

sentences.en: She was working at Intel and living in Silicon Valley.
sentences.zh: 她当时在英特尔工作，住在硅谷。

sentences.en: And these two Stanford grad students named Sergey Brin and Larry Page, they were looking for a place to house their brand new startup, this search engine called Google.
sentences.zh: 这两个名叫谢尔盖·布林和拉里·佩奇的斯坦福研究生，在寻找一个地方来安置他们的全新初创公司，也就是这个名为谷歌的搜索引擎。

sentences.en: And eventually, they convinced her to come over and help them build it as a business.
sentences.zh: 最终，他们说服她过来帮助他们将其实际发展成一项业务。

sentences.en: And she became Google's 16th employee.
sentences.zh: 她成为了谷歌的第16名员工。

sentences.en: And so, you know, then you became history's most successful landlord.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，后来你成了历史上最成功的房东。

sentences.en: And you, you know, you got to Google and started, you know, working in the tech world.
sentences.zh: 而且你，你知道的，来到了谷歌，开始，你知道的，在科技界工作。

sentences.en: And in 2014, you know, made the decision that you were going to come over and run YouTube.
sentences.zh: 然后在2014年，你知道的，作出了决定，你要过来管理YouTube。

sentences.en: And what do you remember about YouTube when you came in?
sentences.zh: 你对刚来时的YouTube有什么记忆？

sentences.en: Like, what was it like?
sentences.zh: 它当时是什么样的？

sentences.en: Well, first of all, you know, when I was first asked whether or not I wanted to have this role, I had been running our advertising business.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，你知道的，当我第一次被问及是否想要担任这个角色时，我一直在管理我们的广告业务。

sentences.en: And so Larry asked me, Larry Page, and I immediately said yes.
sentences.zh: 所以拉里问我，也就是拉里·佩奇，我立刻就答应了。

sentences.en: I have always had a love for the visual arts.
sentences.zh: 我一直对视觉艺术有着热爱。

sentences.en: I was a photographer.
sentences.zh: 我曾是一名摄影师。

sentences.en: I love creative.
sentences.zh: 我热爱创意。

sentences.en: I had created Google's image search.
sentences.zh: 我曾创建了谷歌的图片搜索。

sentences.en: And I could just see clear as day that YouTube had huge potential in front of it.
sentences.zh: 我能清清楚楚地看到YouTube前方有着巨大的潜力。

sentences.en: And so in many ways, I thought, oh, I'll go to YouTube and I'll get to work with all these fun entertainment creators.
sentences.zh: 所以在很多方面，我想，哦，我要去YouTube，我能和所有这些有趣的娱乐创作者一起工作。

sentences.en: It probably seemed like you were going from a very serious job to a very fun job.
sentences.zh: 这可能看起来就像你从一份非常严肃的工作转到了一份非常有趣的工作。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: YouTube at the time was really much more of an entertainment site.
sentences.zh: 那时的YouTube实际上更像是一个娱乐网站。

sentences.en: It was not seen as a very serious site.
sentences.zh: 它不被认为是一个非常严肃的网站。

sentences.en: Yesterday, the Internet blew up over this video of a rat carrying a whole slice of pizza.
sentences.zh: 昨天，互联网因这段老鼠叼着一整片披萨的视频而彻底炸开了锅。

sentences.en: And actually, one of the areas that I really pushed our team a lot on was actually freshness because I would get frustrated.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我真正向团队大力推动的领域之一其实是新鲜感，因为我会感到沮丧。

sentences.en: I would come to YouTube repeatedly and I would keep seeing the same videos.
sentences.zh: 我反复访问YouTube，却总是看到同样的视频。

sentences.en: One of the areas I'd push them on and I've consistently pushed them on is actually exploring new areas, which is, of course, the hardest area for us to discover.
sentences.zh: 我向他们推动的领域之一，也是我一直以来都在推动的，其实是探索新的领域，这当然也是我们最难发现的领域。

sentences.en: Interests that you haven't necessarily told us that you're interested in.
sentences.zh: 你未必告诉过我们你感兴趣的兴趣。

sentences.en: Or that you might not know you're interested in.
sentences.zh: 或者你可能都不知道自己感兴趣。

sentences.en: Or you might not know, but we think they're interesting.
sentences.zh: 或者你可能不知道，但我们认为它们很有趣。

sentences.en: Like that exploratory part is a really important part.
sentences.zh: 像这种探索性的部分是一个非常重要的部分。

sentences.en: And I do think we've gotten better at it.
sentences.zh: 而且我确实认为我们在这一点上做得越来越好了。

sentences.en: And we certainly have gotten better at predicting what people are interested in.
sentences.zh: 我们当然也更擅长预测人们感兴趣的内容。

sentences.en: So part of why I wanted to talk to Susan was to ask her about this 2015-2016 period.
sentences.zh: 所以我想要采访苏珊的部分原因，是想问她关于2015-2016年这段时期的情况。

sentences.en: This period when YouTube was trying to engineer this new algorithm that ended up opening the door to more polarization and extreme views.
sentences.zh: 也就是YouTube试图设计这种新算法的时期，这个算法最终为更多的极端化和极端观点打开了大门。

sentences.en: And was also right when Caleb was getting introduced to all of these new characters.
sentences.zh: 这也是卡勒伯开始接触所有这些新角色的那个时候。

sentences.en: And it was kind of striking that almost right off the bat, she owned the fact that she had driven that change.
sentences.zh: 而且挺让人吃惊的是，几乎一开场，她就承认了是她推动了这一改变。

sentences.en: I want to talk more about the recommendations thing.
sentences.zh: 我想多聊聊推荐系统的事。

sentences.en: As you know, I've been very interested in it.
sentences.zh: 如你所知，我对此一直非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: And one of the people I've talked to and wrote about was a guy named Caleb Kane.
sentences.zh: 我交谈过并撰文报道过的人之一，是个叫卡勒布·凯恩的家伙。

sentences.en: Just like to sort of ask the most blunt possible version of this question.
sentences.zh: 我只想开门见山地问一个最直白的问题。

sentences.en: Like, what did you think of that story?
sentences.zh: 比如，你对那个故事有什么看法？

sentences.en: Um, I mean, I thought of the story, you were trying to understand how our recommendation systems were working and what the impact of them were.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，我想到了这个故事，你当时试图理解我们的推荐系统是如何运作的以及它们的影响是什么。

sentences.en: And that was...
sentences.zh: 而那是……

sentences.en: And what was her take on Caleb's story?
sentences.zh: 她对卡勒布的故事有什么看法？

sentences.en: Well, she, she didn't really get into the specifics of his story, but...
sentences.zh: 嗯，她，她并没有真正深入探讨他故事的细节，但是……

sentences.en: And it wasn't just you.
sentences.zh: 而且不只是你。

sentences.en: There are many people that have raised questions or concerns on how our recommendation systems work.
sentences.zh: 有许多人对我们的推荐系统如何运作提出了质疑或担忧。

sentences.en: And we wanted to make sure we're taking that seriously.
sentences.zh: 我们希望确保我们对此采取了严肃的态度。

sentences.en: She did acknowledge that YouTube had taken from stories like his that they needed to start making some changes.
sentences.zh: 她确实承认，YouTube 从像他这样的故事中认识到，他们需要开始做出一些改变。

sentences.en: And we have taken it seriously.
sentences.zh: 我们确实采取了严肃的态度。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, we've made a lot of changes to how our systems work.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道的，我们对系统的运作方式做出很多改变。

sentences.en: I want to talk about all those changes.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈所有这些改变。

sentences.en: Um, I, but I'm, I'm struck by the fact that you said that one of the challenges for the algorithm and your design of it was getting people to explore new interests.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我，但我，我印象深刻的是，你提到算法及其设计的挑战之一是让人们去探索新的兴趣。

sentences.en: That's, that strikes me as something that, that happened to him where he went to YouTube looking for self-help videos.
sentences.zh: 这让我觉得，这就像发生在他身上的事一样，他去 YouTube 是为了找自助视频。

sentences.en: He was going through a rough patch.
sentences.zh: 他当时正经历一段艰难时期。

sentences.en: He wanted to find something to cheer him up.
sentences.zh: 他想找点能让自己振作起来的东西。

sentences.en: And then he got introduced to these people who would do self-help, but then they would also talk about politics and they would go on each other's shows and they were creating
sentences.zh: 然后他接触到了这些人，他们做自助内容，但他们也会谈论政治，他们会互相上对方的节目，并且他们正在创造

sentences.en: this kind of bridge between like the self-help part of YouTube and the more political part of YouTube.
sentences.zh: 这种桥梁，连接着 YouTube 上的自助部分和更具政治色彩的部分。

sentences.en: Was that something that you observed happening on the platform?
sentences.zh: 这是你在平台上观察到的现象吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it's interesting that you say that because I, I guess I want to say going back from my early initial days, which is that we couldn't get people interested in news or
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你这么说很有趣，因为我，我想说回顾我最初的早期日子，那就是我们无法让人们对新闻感兴趣，或者

sentences.en: get people interested in politics.
sentences.zh: 让人对政治感兴趣。

sentences.en: I don't think we, we had no indication that this was something that people were interested in.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们，我们没有任何迹象表明人们对这感兴趣。

sentences.en: Like people were interested in gaming and music entertainment.
sentences.zh: 就像人们对游戏和音乐娱乐感兴趣一样。

sentences.en: They came to laugh, they came to, to escape in many ways.
sentences.zh: 他们是为了笑而来的，他们是为了在很多方面寻求逃避。

sentences.en: She went back to this idea that YouTube just wasn't seeing data that suggested that people were looking for politics on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 她重申了这种观点，即 YouTube 并没有看到任何数据表明人们在 YouTube 上寻找政治内容。

sentences.en: I acknowledge that there are many political commentators and a lot of political views that have emerged on the platform, but that was not an initial part of how YouTube worked.
sentences.zh: 我承认平台上出现了很多政治评论员和许多政治观点，但这并不是 YouTube 最初运作方式的一部分。

sentences.en: And I guess the only reason I'm bringing that up, because I do want to say that, you know,
sentences.zh: 我想我提起这事的唯一原因，是因为我确实想说，你知道的，

sentences.en: YouTube for all its creators, for, you know, million, millions of creators, there is a set of creators who do find success with that, but it's a small set.
sentences.zh: YouTube 对于所有的创作者来说，对于，你知道的，成百上千万的创作者来说，有一部分创作者确实在这上面取得了成功，但只是一小部分。

sentences.en: And in the end, she said that essentially like this kind of political content, it's still a really small percentage of everything else on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 最后，她表示，基本上这种政治内容仍然只占 YouTube 上所有内容的极小一部分。

sentences.en: And is that true?
sentences.zh: 那是真的吗？

sentences.en: Like, cause it seems like, it seems like there's a lot of it, I guess.
sentences.zh: 因为，感觉好像，感觉这种内容很多，我想。

sentences.en: I mean, there's no way to know for sure without having access to their internal data.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在无法访问他们内部数据的情况下，没有办法确切知道。

sentences.en: But like, even if it were true that only 1% of YouTube videos consisted of this kind of
sentences.zh: 但就像，即使 1% 的 YouTube 视频包含这种

sentences.en: political content, because YouTube is so big, that would still translate to millions and millions of people around the world watching it.
sentences.zh: 政治内容是真的，因为 YouTube 太大了，这仍然意味着全世界有数百万人在观看。

sentences.en: And we've talked to some people who were at YouTube earlier in its history around the time that you
sentences.zh: 我们和一些在 YouTube 早期（也就是你

sentences.en: came and even before then, who said, you know, that there was sort of this obsession with growth,
sentences.zh: 来的时候甚至更早）呆过的人聊过，他们说，你知道的，当时对增长有一种迷恋，

sentences.en: that there was a very strong push to expand the watch time on the platform, and that any challenges that were brought to management around that, that these things were just weren't
sentences.zh: 有一种非常强烈的推动力去扩大平台上的观看时长，任何向管理层提出的关于这方面的质疑，这些事情根本就

sentences.en: given a real hearing.
sentences.zh: 没有得到真正的听取。

sentences.en: Does that resonate with you at all?
sentences.zh: 这引起你的共鸣了吗？

sentences.en: And I asked about Guillaume, too, about the red flags that he had tried to raise back when he was at YouTube.
sentences.zh: 我还问了纪尧姆的事，关于他在 YouTube 期间试图敲响的警钟。

sentences.en: I mean, I think I've certainly heard people say that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我当然听过人们这么说。

sentences.en: And, um, I, I mean, you know, like, I came from a company that was very focused on quality, quality of information.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，我，我的意思是，你知道，我来自一家非常专注于质量的公司，也就是信息的质量。

sentences.en: It was always like the most important thing we also always prioritized was quality.
sentences.zh: 这总是最重要的事情，我们一直优先考虑的也是质量。

sentences.en: And she didn't really deny it, but she pivoted pretty fast to her work at Google and this concept of quality, which is basically like the term that Google uses to talk about its
sentences.zh: 她并没有真正否认这一点，但她相当快地把话题转向了她在谷歌的工作以及“质量”这个概念，这基本上就像是谷歌用来指代其

sentences.en: search engine and how it wants people to get good, reliable information when they go looking for something.
sentences.zh: 搜索引擎的术语，以及它如何希望人们在寻找东西时获得优质、可靠的信息。

sentences.en: And so I tried to figure out how do you reconcile that with a company that is a more entertainment based company, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我试图弄清楚，你如何将这一点与一家更偏向娱乐的公司调和起来呢？

sentences.en: So what does that mean to have quality if the main thing that you're doing is gaming videos, cat videos and music videos?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果你的主要业务是游戏视频、猫咪视频和音乐视频，拥有质量意味着什么？

sentences.en: Then what does that really mean for quality?
sentences.zh: 那对质量来说到底意味着什么？

sentences.en: And I think what she's getting at is that at the time, like YouTube just didn't really think that it was capable of doing much harm.
sentences.zh: 我想她的意思是，当时，YouTube 真的不觉得自己有能力造成多大危害。

sentences.en: And I, I, I guess the reason I'm bringing that up is that one of the biggest realizations for me was
sentences.zh: 而且，我，我，我想我提起这件事的原因是，对我和最大的认识之一就是

sentences.en: that we needed to start adapting and changing and that we needed a very different set of ways of managing information than you want to manage entertainment.
sentences.zh: 我们需要开始适应和改变，并且我们需要一套与管理娱乐完全不同的信息管理方式。

sentences.en: Was there a moment that crystallized that for you?
sentences.zh: 有没有哪个时刻让你对此有了深刻的认识？

sentences.en: Um, well, it's the moment celebration became nightmare.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是庆祝变成噩梦的时刻。

sentences.en: In 2016, people were screaming, kids were crying.
sentences.zh: 2016 年，人们在尖叫，孩子们在哭泣。

sentences.en: There was a terrorist attack that had happened in France.
sentences.zh: 法国发生了一起恐怖袭击。

sentences.en: Horror tonight in the French resort town of Nice.
sentences.zh: 今晚法国度假小镇尼斯发生恐怖事件。

sentences.en: Susan says that in 2016 on Bastille Day.
sentences.zh: 苏珊说那是 2016 年的巴士底日。

sentences.en: In the coastal city of Nice, just as the fireworks ended, a truck plowed into the crowd.
sentences.zh: 在沿海城市尼斯，就在烟花结束时，一辆卡车冲入人群。

sentences.en: When an ISIS terrorist attacked a crowd.
sentences.zh: 当一名伊斯兰国恐怖分子袭击人群时。

sentences.en: At least 84 people were killed.
sentences.zh: 至少 84 人死亡。

sentences.en: Dozens of others were hurt.
sentences.zh: 数十人受伤。

sentences.en: And the government there declared a state of emergency.
sentences.zh: 那里的政府宣布进入紧急状态。

sentences.en: And I remember reading that and being, you know, just extremely upset and thinking, our users need to know about it.
sentences.zh: 我记得读到这个消息时，你知道的，感到极其沮丧，心想我们的用户需要知道这件事。

sentences.en: YouTube decided that for people in France, it was actually going to push news about the attack onto their homepages.
sentences.zh: YouTube 决定对法国的用户，实际上要将关于袭击的新闻推送至他们的主页上。

sentences.en: The attack turned the streets into a scene of chaos.
sentences.zh: 袭击将街道变成了一片混乱的景象。

sentences.en: And for people looking for information about the attack.
sentences.zh: 对于寻找有关袭击信息的人来说。

sentences.en: The mayor of Nice warning people to stay indoors.
sentences.zh: 尼斯市长警告人们待在室内。

sentences.en: Here's tonight of another terror attack.
sentences.zh: 今晚又发生了一起恐怖袭击。

sentences.en: They were actually going to prioritize videos from what they considered authoritative sources.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上将优先展示来自他们认为具有权威性的来源的视频。

sentences.en: But that didn't perform very well on our platform.
sentences.zh: 但这在我们的平台上表现得并不好。

sentences.en: She says that basically the engineers at YouTube were telling her like.
sentences.zh: 她说，基本上 YouTube 的工程师告诉她：

sentences.en: The users don't want to actually see it.
sentences.zh: 用户其实并不想看到这个。

sentences.en: No one is clicking on these videos.
sentences.zh: 没有人点击这些视频。

sentences.en: That's just not what they want to see.
sentences.zh: 这根本不是他们想看的内容。

sentences.en: And so what do you do as a platform?
sentences.zh: 作为一个平台，你该怎么做？

sentences.en: Do you show it to them anyway?
sentences.zh: 无论如何都要展示给他们看吗？

sentences.en: And so that's actually, I remember that very clearly because that was the first time I said to them, you know, it doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，我对此记忆犹新，因为那是第一次我对他们说，这没关系。

sentences.en: We have a responsibility.
sentences.zh: 我们有责任。

sentences.en: Something happened in the world and it's important for our users to know.
sentences.zh: 世界上发生了事情，让我们的用户了解是很重要的。

sentences.en: And according to her, she said basically like, too bad.
sentences.zh: 据她所说，她基本上说：真糟糕。

sentences.en: We're showing it to them anyway.
sentences.zh: 无论如何我们都要展示给他们看。

sentences.en: And it was the first time we started using the word responsibility.
sentences.zh: 这是我们第一次开始使用“责任”这个词。

sentences.en: And the fact that we needed to put information that in our site that was relevant,
sentences.zh: 而且我们需要在我们的网站上放置相关信息的现实情况是，

sentences.en: even if our users were not necessarily engaging with it in the same way that they would with the entertainment videos.
sentences.zh: 即使我们的用户不一定会像对待娱乐视频那样去参与其中。

sentences.en: So if I'm understanding this right,
sentences.zh: 如果我没理解错的话，

sentences.en: what Susan is saying is that the Nice attack marked the first time that YouTube took this idea of responsibility and prioritized that over watch time.
sentences.zh: 苏珊所说的是，尼斯袭击事件标志着 YouTube 首次将这种责任感置于观看时长之上。

sentences.en: At what point did that sense of responsibility extend beyond like a big news event?
sentences.zh: 这种责任感是在什么时候从重大新闻事件扩展开来的呢？

sentences.en: It took a little while.
sentences.zh: 这花了点时间。

sentences.en: I mean, I think over 2017 and 18 and into 2019, I think pressure was starting to build on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为在 2017、2018 乃至 2019 年，我认为 YouTube 面临的压力开始增加。

sentences.en: CNN reports that YouTube ran ads from large brands like Adidas, Amazon and Hershey before videos which promoted extreme content.
sentences.zh: 美国有线电视新闻网报道称，YouTube 在宣传极端内容的视频前播放了阿迪达斯、亚马逊和好时等大品牌的广告。

sentences.en: There were reports in the Times and other places.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》和其他地方都有相关报道。

sentences.en: You're about to meet a man who says he was radicalized by alt-right figures via their persuasive YouTube videos.
sentences.zh: 你即将见到一个人，他说自己被极右翼人物通过他们极具说服力的 YouTube 视频洗脑了。

sentences.en: Regulators, parents.
sentences.zh: 监管机构，家长们。

sentences.en: YouTube is one of the greatest engines of extremism that we might have ever created at this scale.
sentences.zh: YouTube 是我们在这个规模上创造过的最强大的极端主义助推器之一。

sentences.en: Advertisers, they were all chiming in.
sentences.zh: 广告商，他们都在发声。

sentences.en: Good morning, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家早上好。

sentences.en: The Subcommittee on Consumer Protection and Commerce will now come to order.
sentences.zh: 消费者保护和商业小组委员会现在开会。

sentences.en: Congress actually held hearings about these Internet platforMs.
sentences.zh: 国会实际上就这些互联网平台举行了听证会。

sentences.en: Congress has unfortunately taken a laissez-faire approach to regulation of unfair and deceptive practices online over the past decade.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，在过去的十年里，国会采取了一种自由放任的方法来监管网上的不公平和欺骗行为。

sentences.en: And platforms have let them flourish.
sentences.zh: 而平台则任由它们滋生。

sentences.en: And invited experts, including former Google employees.
sentences.zh: 并邀请了专家，包括前谷歌员工。

sentences.en: So there you are.
sentences.zh: 所以你来了。

sentences.en: You're about to hit play in a YouTube video.
sentences.zh: 你正准备点击播放一个 YouTube 视频。

sentences.en: And you hit play.
sentences.zh: 然后你点击了播放。

sentences.en: And then you think you're going to watch this one video.
sentences.zh: 然后你以为你只会看这一个视频。

sentences.en: And then you wake up two hours later and say, oh my God, what just happened?
sentences.zh: 结果两个小时后你醒来，说，天哪，刚才发生了什么？

sentences.en: And the answer is because you had a supercomputer pointed at your brain.
sentences.zh: 答案是，因为你有一台超级计算机正对准你的大脑。

sentences.en: To talk about how YouTube was essentially built to pull people into these polarizing rabbit holes.
sentences.zh: 来谈谈 YouTube 基本上是如何被构建来将人们拉入这些两极分化的兔子洞的。

sentences.en: It's sad to me because it's happening not by accident, but by design.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到悲哀，因为这不是偶然发生的，而是刻意设计的。

sentences.en: And that's when YouTube started making these big changes last year.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，YouTube 在去年开始做出这些重大的改变。

sentences.en: They disappeared me.
sentences.zh: 他们把我“消失”了。

sentences.en: So I've just been told I'm on double secret probation.
sentences.zh: 所以我刚被告知我处于双重秘密留用察看期。

sentences.en: Apparently, you see, I had violated community standards.
sentences.zh: 显然，你看，我违反了社区准则。

sentences.en: You know, one of the biggest changes that we made from our recommendation system, and it was probably one of the later changes we made,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们对推荐系统做出的最大改变之一，可能也是我们较晚做出的改变之一，

sentences.en: and I think it's because it's a harder one to grapple, which is that we realized that there was a set of content
sentences.zh: 我想这是因为它是一个更难处理的问题，那就是我们意识到存在这样一组内容，

sentences.en: that even if people were repeatedly engaging with it, we thought it was important to make the recommendations more diversified and to show them more quality content alongside.
sentences.zh: 即使用户反复与之互动，我们也认为有必要让推荐更加多元化，并在旁边向他们展示更多高质量的内容。

sentences.en: What she's essentially said is that there's a certain kind of video where, like, even if a lot of people are watching it and it's generating all this viewing time,
sentences.zh: 她本质上所说的是，存在某种特定类型的视频，比如说，即使很多人在看，而且它创造了所有的观看时间，

sentences.en: the site will actually intervene.
sentences.zh: 网站实际上也会进行干预。

sentences.en: You know, if a video has hate speech in it or if it's made by, like, a neo-Nazi who's denying the Holocaust happened, that will come totally down off YouTube.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果一个视频包含仇恨言论，或者是由否认大屠杀的新纳粹分子制作的，那将被彻底从 YouTube 上清除。

sentences.en: But there's this other class of videos that YouTube has a harder time categorizing.
sentences.zh: 但还有另一类视频，YouTube 很难对其进行分类。

sentences.en: You know, we began to identify content that we called borderline content and that if users were repeatedly engaging with this borderline content,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们开始识别我们称之为“边缘内容”的内容，如果用户反复与这种边缘内容互动，

sentences.en: we will show them other content alongside that we've ranked as more high-quality content.
sentences.zh: 我们就会在旁边向他们展示我们评级为更高质量的其他内容。

sentences.en: And these videos, like, they don't explicitly violate YouTube's rules, but they're also, like, not the kind of thing that YouTube wants to boost and recommend.
sentences.zh: 这些视频，比如，它们没有明确违反 YouTube 的规则，但它们也，比如，不是 YouTube 想要推动和推荐的那种东西。

sentences.en: So what they've done is essentially to train algorithms to identify these kinds of videos
sentences.zh: 所以他们所做的基本上是训练算法来识别这些类型的视频，

sentences.en: and then demote them in people's feeds and in their sidebars so that they don't get seen as often.
sentences.zh: 然后在人们的信息流和侧边栏中将它们降权，这样它们就不会经常被看到了。

sentences.en: And what that has done is it's actually had a 70% reduction of views of borderline content in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而这所带来的结果是，在美国，边缘内容的观看量实际上减少了 70%。

sentences.en: And we've been in the process of rolling that out globally.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在全球范围内推广这一功能。

sentences.en: It's in most English-language countries right now and a few large markets like France and Germany, but we continue to roll that out.
sentences.zh: 目前它已在大多数英语国家以及法国和德国等少数主要市场推出，但我们仍在继续推广。

sentences.en: And how do you define, like, borderline content?
sentences.zh: 那你怎么定义，比如边缘内容？

sentences.en: Like, what's borderline versus just, you know, edgy jokes?
sentences.zh: 比如，什么是边缘内容，而什么又只是，你知道的，出格的笑话？

sentences.en: How do you sort of separate the two?
sentences.zh: 你们是如何区分这两者的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it is a complicated and nuanced area.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个复杂且微妙的领域。

sentences.en: And, I mean, we have a whole process and algorithm to find it.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，我们有一整套流程和算法来找到它。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I guess what I'm wondering is, like, these are sort of interventions in an automated system, right?
sentences.zh: 我想我在想的是，这些有点像是对自动化系统的干预，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, you set up this automated system, let it run, realized, like, some of the things that it produces,
sentences.zh: 就像，你建立这个自动化系统，让它运行，意识到，比如它产生的一些东西，

sentences.en: realized that maybe those aren't creating an optimal experience for people, and then, you know, humans come in and sort of tinker with it to produce different results.
sentences.zh: 意识到这些可能没有为人们创造最佳体验，然后，你知道的，人类介入并对其进行修补以产生不同的结果。

sentences.en: Do you feel like when you—
sentences.zh: 你觉得当你——

sentences.en: Well, hopefully we do more than tinker.
sentences.zh: 嗯，希望我们的所作所为不仅仅是修修补补。

sentences.en: Well, right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对。

sentences.en: We, like, have a lot of advanced technology and we work very scientifically to make sure we do it right.
sentences.zh: 我们，比如，拥有许多先进的技术，并且我们以非常科学的方式工作，以确保我们做对了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I guess a sort of overarching question is, do you think there was an over-reliance in YouTube's early days on automation, on machines?
sentences.zh: 我想一个总括性的问题是，你认为 YouTube 在早期是否过分依赖自动化、依赖机器？

sentences.en: Like, do you think there was a sort of underappreciation for the role that sort of judgment and human intuition played in this stuff?
sentences.zh: 比如，你认为是否有点低估了判断力和人类直觉在这类事情中所起的作用？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: I mean, I think both are really important.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为两者都非常重要。

sentences.en: And if we look at how our systems work, we definitely have a lot of—we have basically a system that is very heavy with humans that is extended with machines.
sentences.zh: 如果我们看看系统的运作方式，我们确实有很多……基本上我们的系统很大程度上依赖人类，并由机器来延伸。

sentences.en: There is an automated component, but then there's also, of course, a human component.
sentences.zh: 其中有自动化组件，但当然也有人类组件。

sentences.en: So, is she saying that humans are now doing more work than the AI?
sentences.zh: 所以，她是说人类现在比AI做更多的工作吗？

sentences.en: No.

sentences.en: I mean, like, yeah, like, they do have more people looking at videos than they used to.

sentences.en: We have a number of raters that all watch and review videos.
sentences.zh: 我们有许多评估员，都在观看和审核视频。

sentences.en: And based on the feedback, we identify a set of content that looks borderline.
sentences.zh: 根据反馈，我们识别出一批处于边缘的内容。

sentences.en: But YouTube is so big, they could hire a hundred times as many people,
sentences.zh: 但YouTube太大了，就算他们雇佣一百倍的人数，

sentences.en: and they still wouldn't be able to watch a fraction of everything that's being uploaded to YouTube on any given day.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然无法看完每天上传到YouTube的所有内容的冰山一角。

sentences.en: So, it's still the case, then, that most videos that I'm recommended, that anyone who goes to YouTube is recommended,

sentences.en: those recommendations are coming from different algorithms being run by an artificial intelligence.
sentences.zh: 这些推荐都来自于人工智能运行的不同算法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The robots are still very much running the show.
sentences.zh: 机器人依然在很大程度上掌控着一切。

sentences.en: But what she's saying is that they're trying to give humans a bigger role in supervising them.
sentences.zh: 但她所说的是，他们正试图让场外人类在监督它们方面发挥更大的作用。

sentences.zh: 你可能看不到安德烈亚，但她正在把我们挥走，不过我们，能再给我们几分钟吗？

sentences.en: We're good?
sentences.zh: 我们没问题吧？

sentences.en: Okay, well, we'll start wrapping it up.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那我们准备收尾了。

sentences.zh: 我确实还有几个问题。

sentences.zh: 一个是，我想问问2018年这里发生的枪击事件。

sentences.en: I wonder what that was like for you.
sentences.zh: 我想知道对你来说那是什么样的经历。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, it was, first of all, just a horrible event to go through.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，首先，这只是一场可怕的经历。

sentences.en: We have a report of subject with a gun.
sentences.zh: 我们接到有持枪嫌疑人的报警。

sentences.en: This will be from the YouTube building.
sentences.zh: 地点在YouTube大楼。

sentences.en: Like, when something like that happens to you, you can't really process that it's happening.
sentences.zh: 当这种事发生在你身上时，你真的无法去消化它正在发生。

sentences.en: A flood of YouTube employees streaming out toward safety, some still clutching tightly to their laptops.
sentences.zh: 大批YouTube员工涌向安全地带，有些人手里还紧紧抓着笔记本电脑。

sentences.en: Turning what was an ordinary, normal lunch hour on this tech campus into an all-too-familiar shooting scene in America.
sentences.zh: 这把这个科技园区里一个平凡普通的午餐时间，变成了一场在美国再熟悉不过的枪击现场。

sentences.en: You don't know, is there one shooter?
sentences.zh: 你不知道，是一个枪手吗？

sentences.zh: 是有五个枪手吗？

sentences.en: Where are they?
sentences.zh: 他们在哪里？

sentences.en: New details about the woman police say shot three people at YouTube's headquarters before taking her own life.
sentences.zh: 关于警方称在YouTube总部开枪打伤三人后自杀的女性的新细节。

sentences.en: I'm being discriminated and filtered on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 我在YouTube上受到歧视和过滤。

sentences.zh: 我以前获得很多观看次数的老视频不再有观看次数了。

sentences.en: Accusing the website of filtering her channels to keep her videos from getting views.
sentences.zh: 指责该网站过滤她的频道，阻止她的视频获得观看次数。

sentences.en: Something she blames on new, closed-minded YouTube employees.
sentences.zh: 她将此归咎于YouTube新来的、思想狭隘的员工。

sentences.en: I'm very thankful in some ways that nobody was killed.
sentences.zh: 从某些方面来说，我很庆幸没有人丧生。

sentences.en: I think it also just showed any kind of information company has some risk of people being upset with information that's reported.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也表明，任何类型的信息公司都有人对所报道的信息感到不满的风险。

sentences.en: And so, you know, my key takeaway was that we need to make sure that our employees are always safe and that we're doing everything we possibly can.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我的核心体会是，我们需要确保我们的员工始终安全，并且我们在尽一切可能做到最好。

sentences.en: And I wonder, was that a moment for you where you realized the stakes of the decisions you made here in a different way?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，那对你来说是一个以不同方式意识到你在这里所做决定利害关系的时刻吗？

sentences.en: Did it change the way you looked at your responsibility?
sentences.zh: 它改变了你对责任的看法吗？

sentences.en: I mean, information is a tough business.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，信息是一个艰难的行业。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，

sentences.en: you are in the information business yourselves and you understand that sometimes people can get really upset and they can get really angry about ways that they're covered or ways that information is displayed.
sentences.zh: 你们自己也身处新闻信息行业，你们明白，有时人们会对报道方式或信息的展示方式感到非常不满和愤怒。

sentences.en: And just like a journalistic organization like yourselves, you need to do what's right.
sentences.zh: 就像你们这样的新闻机构一样，你们需要做正确的事。

sentences.en: I want to look back on this time and feel that I made the right decisions.
sentences.zh: 我想回顾这段时间，并觉得自己做出了正确的决定。

sentences.en: I don't want to say, oh, I allowed this type of content because I was afraid.
sentences.zh: 我不想说，哦，我允许这种类型的内容，因为我害怕。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, I remember sort of that day and, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我还记得那天，你知道，

sentences.en: other shootings since that day and that have been sort of related in some way to the Internet and just feeling like a sense of loss.
sentences.zh: 以及那之后的其他枪击事件，那些在某种程度上与互联网有关的事件，就有一种失落感。

sentences.en: Like I grew up on the Internet.
sentences.zh: 就像我是伴随着互联网长大的。

sentences.en: I love the Internet.
sentences.zh: 我热爱互联网。

sentences.en: I have wondered if we're ever going to get back to a time when these things feel fun and useful and like they're not leading to these culture wars and polarization.
sentences.zh: 我一直在想，我们是否还能回到这样一个时代：这些东西感觉既有趣又有用，而且不会导致文化战争和两极分化。

sentences.en: Like, do you think that we'll ever feel like that about the Internet again?
sentences.zh: 比如，你认为我们对互联网还会再有这种感觉吗？

sentences.en: I love the Internet.
sentences.zh: 我热爱互联网。

sentences.en: I think that the Internet has enabled so many different opportunities for people that wouldn't have had it.
sentences.zh: 我认为互联网为那些本来没有机会的人提供了如此多的不同机会。

sentences.en: And I think you're right.
sentences.zh: 我想你是对的。

sentences.en: Like in the last couple of years, there's been a lot of scrutiny.
sentences.zh: 就像在过去几年里，有很多审视。

sentences.en: And it's because of the size that we are and because people realize the significance of our platform.
sentences.zh: 这是因为我们的规模以及人们意识到我们平台的重要性。

sentences.en: And I recognize that and I take that very seriously.
sentences.zh: 我认识到了这一点，并且非常认真地对待它。

sentences.en: My focus on responsibility is is probably one of the most important things I'll do in my life.
sentences.zh: 我对责任的关注可能是我一生中最重要的事情之一。

sentences.en: And why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Because we I think we live at this time where there's tremendous change.
sentences.zh: 因为我们，我认为我们生活在一个发生巨大变化的时代。

sentences.en: And so, yes, we've had years of all this fun and gaming and cat videos.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我们经历过多年充满乐趣、游戏和猫咪视频的时光。

sentences.en: But there are a lot of really important decisions to be made about what this future will hold and what will platforms be and how will they operate in the future.
sentences.zh: 但对于这个未来将承载什么、平台将是什么以及它们未来将如何运营，还有很多非常重要的决定需要做出。

sentences.en: And those rules haven't been written yet or we're in the process of writing them.
sentences.zh: 而这些规则尚未书写，或者我们正处于书写它们的过程中。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Well, thank you.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.zh: 谢谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: Thank you.

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.zh: 她说YouTube一直在以最快的速度积极搜寻并删除这些内容。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Dr. John Brooks with the CDC.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是美国疾病控制与预防中心的约翰·布鲁克斯医生。

sentences.en: We put links to the CDC.
sentences.zh: 我们在视频中加入了指向疾控中心的链接。

sentences.en: Hello, everyone, and welcome to this regular press conference on COVID-19 from Geneva.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎收看这场在日内瓦举行的关于新冠肺炎的例行新闻发布会。

sentences.en: The World Health Organization or to the Associated Equivalent globally in the home feed under videos that were about coronavirus and in our searches.
sentences.zh: 世界卫生组织或全球相应的权威机构，会出现在关于新冠病毒的视频下方的首页推荐以及我们的搜索结果中。

sentences.en: Let's work together to keep ourselves healthy, our families healthy, and our communities healthy.
sentences.zh: 让我们共同努力，保持我们自己、我们的家庭和我们的社区健康。

sentences.en: On every video about the coronavirus, they like put this little link that directs people to like the CDC's website or other health authorities.
sentences.zh: 在每一条关于新冠病毒的视频上，他们都会放置一个小链接，引导人们访问疾控中心或其他卫生机构的网站。

sentences.en: So the 5G story is complete and utter rubbish.
sentences.zh: 所以关于5G的说法完全是无稽之谈。

sentences.en: It's nonsense.
sentences.zh: 这纯属无谈。

sentences.en: It's the worst kind of fake news.
sentences.zh: 这是最恶劣的假新闻。

sentences.en: We have a new shelf that we launched that gives users information from authoritative sources.
sentences.zh: 我们推出了一个新专栏，为用户提供来自权威机构的信息。

sentences.en: Far-fetched conspiracy theories like this are really damaging because they undermine public health efforts to stop the spread of the virus by convincing some people that it's not the real problem.
sentences.zh: 像这样荒诞的阴谋论真的具有极大的破坏力，因为它们说服了一些人相信这不是真正的问题，从而破坏了阻止病毒传播的公共卫生努力。

sentences.en: They created this feature that basically, like, when you search for information about the coronavirus,
sentences.zh: 他们创造了这个功能，基本上就是，当你在搜索关于新冠病毒的信息时，

sentences.en: the first thing you see is this section called top news that contains essentially like information from authoritative trusted sources.
sentences.zh: 你首先看到的是一个叫做头条新闻的板块，里面基本上包含了来自权威可信源的信息。

sentences.en: Staying inside saves lives.
sentences.zh: 呆在室内就是拯救生命。

sentences.en: Stay home.
sentences.zh: 呆在家时。

sentences.en: They also got popular YouTubers to make these social distancing PSAs.
sentences.zh: 他们还请来热门的YouTuber来制作这些关于保持社交距离的公益广告。

sentences.en: I really think togetherness is the superpower of our species.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为团结是我们这个物种的超能力。

sentences.en: Let's do it together.
sentences.zh: 让我们一起行动吧。

sentences.en: We will keep each other company.
sentences.zh: 我们将彼此陪伴。

sentences.en: So they weren't just hearing it from YouTube.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不只是从YouTube听到这些。

sentences.en: They were hearing it from their favorite creator.
sentences.zh: 他们是从自己最喜爱的创作者那里听到这些的。

sentences.en: Coming over with me.
sentences.zh: 和我一起过来。

sentences.en: Each day can be a different thing.
sentences.zh: 每天都可以是不同的一天。

sentences.en: Which they then promoted to all their subscribers.
sentences.zh: 然后他们将这些内容推广给他们所有的订阅者。

sentences.en: And when we looked at the combined number of subscribers that they have, it's over 1.5 billion subscribers.
sentences.zh: 当我们查看他们拥有的订阅者总数时，超过了15亿订阅者。

sentences.en: You can slow the growth of this and save lives.
sentences.zh: 你可以减缓病毒的传播并拯救生命。

sentences.en: We have everyone at YouTube working throughout this crisis to make sure that they are following what's happening, making changes on the policy,
sentences.zh: 在这场危机期间，YouTube的所有员工都在努力工作，确保他们跟进正在发生的事情，对政策进行调整，

sentences.en: making sure that we are taking down content, making sure that we're adjusting whatever changes we need to our algorithm.
sentences.zh: 确保我们下架内容，确保我们对算法进行任何必要的更改。

sentences.en: And as she's going through her list of everything that YouTube is doing on the coronavirus,
sentences.zh: 当她讲完YouTube为应对新冠病毒所做的一切时，

sentences.en: it really strikes me like how much work it takes to make sure that this algorithm that YouTube has built, that it's not leading people in a dangerous direction.
sentences.zh: 我真的深感震惊，YouTube建立的这个算法要确保不把人们引向危险的方向，究竟需要付出多大的努力。

sentences.en: I mean, I could go on.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我还可以说下去。

sentences.en: We did a lot of different steps here to make sure we were doing everything possible.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里采取了许多不同的步骤，以确保我们做了一切可能做的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, just personally, like, I've been impressed by how hard it's been to find misinformation about the coronavirus on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，仅就个人而言，比如，在YouTube上很难找到关于新冠病毒的虚假信息，这让我印象深刻。

sentences.en: And I guess I'm wondering, like, why isn't it always like this?
sentences.zh: 我想我在想，为什么不是什么时候都这样呢？

sentences.en: Like, what is preventing YouTube from taking this approach all the time to every subject?
sentences.zh: 比如，是什么阻碍了YouTube对所有主题一直采取这种方法？

sentences.en: Well, we do take a responsibility approach to everything that we do.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对于我们所做的每一件事，我们确实都采取了负责任的方法。

sentences.en: What's a little bit different about this one is there is a very clear authority, which is a world health organization.
sentences.zh: 这一个有点不同的是，有一个非常明确的权威机构，那就是世界卫生组织。

sentences.en: And there are recommendations that health organizations are making.
sentences.zh: 并且卫生机构正在提出建议。

sentences.en: And as a result, it's very clear to us that anything that would contradict social distancing, for example, would be a violation of our policies.
sentences.zh: 因此，对我们来说非常明确的是，任何违背社交距离规定的行为，例如，都将违反我们的政策。

sentences.en: And in a lot of other areas, there may be some agreement on the science, but there could be politically different views.
sentences.zh: 而在许多其他领域，科学界可能会有一些共识，但可能会有不同的政治观点。

sentences.en: And so we want to enable a broad range of views.
sentences.zh: 所以我们希望支持广泛的观点。

sentences.en: So Susan's saying that she's basically comfortable doing this kind of work when it comes to something like the coronavirus,
sentences.zh: 所以苏珊的意思是，当涉及到像新冠病毒这样的事情时，她基本上乐意做这种工作，

sentences.en: because it's just science and there are clear authority figures to turn to.
sentences.zh: 因为这只是科学，并且有明确的权威人物可以求助。

sentences.en: But politics is a completely different story.
sentences.zh: 但政治完全是另一码事。

sentences.en: And maybe there's some obvious answer to this, but like, why is that?
sentences.zh: 也许这有一个显而易见的答案，但是，为什么会这样呢？

sentences.en: We want to enable a broad range of views.
sentences.zh: 我们希望支持广泛的观点。

sentences.en: We want to make sure that the full spectrum of political views or social ideas are represented there.
sentences.zh: 我们希望确保政治观点或社会理念的全谱系都能在那里得到代表。

sentences.en: But in this case, it's very clear that there's an authority and information behind that authority.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，很明显有一个权威，以及该权威背后的信息。

sentences.en: I mean, I think on an ideological level, there are a lot of people at YouTube who still want it to be this open platform where every kind of view is welcome and is equal.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为在意识形态层面上，YouTube上仍然有很多人希望它成为一个开放的平台，在这个平台上，各种观点都受欢迎且是平等的。

sentences.en: And I think there's also this more practical angle to it, which is that they don't want to be seen as putting their thumb on the scale.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为还有一个更现实的角度，那就是他们不想被视为在天平上倾向某一方。

sentences.en: They don't want politicians and regulators, people who might try to break them up or enforce new rules on them to think that they're taking a partisan stand.
sentences.zh: 他们不希望政客和监管机构，以及那些可能试图拆分他们或对他们强制实施新规则的人，认为他们在表明党派立场。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But I feel like because of the time that we're living in,
sentences.zh: 但我觉得由于我们所处的时代，

sentences.en: in part due to Internet platforms like YouTube and the powerful AIs that have been designed to capture and keep our attention at all costs,
sentences.zh: 部分原因是像YouTube这样的互联网平台，以及那些旨在不惜一切代价捕获并留住我们注意力的强大AI，

sentences.en: that like now everything feels polarizing and political, even everything around the coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 现在一切都让人感觉两极分化且充满政治色彩，甚至连关于新冠病毒的一切也是如此。

sentences.en: And so it sounds like Susan is saying, you know, okay, we recognize that we helped let this genie out of the bottle.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来苏珊是在说，你知道，好吧，我们承认我们放出了这个魔鬼。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We didn't mean to.
sentences.zh: 我们不是故意的。

sentences.en: We were just trying to entertain.
sentences.zh: 我们只是想娱乐大众。

sentences.en: We're now going to try and put it back.
sentences.zh: 我们现在要试着把它装回去。

sentences.en: But I just wonder, like, in the environment that they helped to create, if that is even possible.
sentences.zh: 但我只是在想，在他们帮助创造的环境中，这是否真的可能。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's kind of a reckoning for them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这对他们来说算是一次清算。

sentences.en: YouTube is part of Google.
sentences.zh: YouTube是谷歌的一部分。

sentences.en: And I've been at Google for over 20 years now.
sentences.zh: 我在谷歌工作已经超过20年了。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's an information company, which means our goal, our mission is to deliver users the most relevant information.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一家信息公司，这意味着我们的目标、我们的使命是向用户提供最相关的信息。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that it's accurate.
sentences.zh: 而且这些信息必须是准确的。

sentences.en: And that's true for YouTube, too, that we want to deliver accurate, useful information.
sentences.zh: 这对YouTube来说也是一样的，我们希望提供准确、有用的信息。

sentences.en: And I think in the information area, it's very important.
sentences.zh: 我认为在信息领域，这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I guess it strikes me as like there's a trust crisis right now.
sentences.zh: 我想这让我觉得现在存在着一场信任危机。

sentences.en: I mean, people just they don't trust necessarily the institutions that maybe they would have years ago to sort of give them accurate information.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们只是不再必然信任那些他们多年前可能会信任的机构来为他们提供准确的信息。

sentences.en: So you're kind of trying to rebuild trust, it strikes me, like, you know, placing content from organizations like the CDC and the WHO prominently on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 所以你有点在试图重建信任，给我的感觉是，你知道，将来自疾控中心和世卫组织等机构的内容显眼地放在YouTube上。

sentences.en: Do you feel like that's part of what you're trying to do right now is to kind of help people on YouTube understand that they actually can trust these sort of mainstream authorities?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这是你现在正在努力做的一部分吗，是为了帮助YouTube上的用户明白他们实际上可以信任这些主流权威？

sentences.en: Well, part of what we want to do for YouTube is make sure that we have all of the voices represented on the platform.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们希望为YouTube做的事情之一，是确保我们在平台上代表了所有的声音。

sentences.en: And YouTube started out with a lot of individuals just posting videos about what was happening in their lives.
sentences.zh: YouTube最初有很多个人只是发布关于他们生活中发生的事情的视频。

sentences.en: But what we've really done over the last couple of years is reach out to make sure that news organizations,
sentences.zh: 但在过去几年里，我们真正做的是伸出援手，确保新闻机构、

sentences.en: trusted scientific health government officials all also have the resources needed to be able to come onto the platform on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 受信任的科学、健康、政府官员也拥有所需的资源，能够来到YouTube这个平台上。

sentences.en: And what I've seen happen with COVID-19 is it's really accelerated public health officials,
sentences.zh: 我在COVID-19上看到的情况是，它确实加速了公共卫生官员的步伐，

sentences.en: recognizing that YouTube is an important medium to be communicating with users about anything involving health.
sentences.zh: 他们认识到YouTube是一个与用户就任何涉及健康的事进行沟通的重要媒介。

sentences.en: And so, you know, in many ways, I think this would have happened naturally.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，在很多方面，我认为这本来会自然发生的。

sentences.en: It might have taken a few years.
sentences.zh: 可能需要几年时间。

sentences.en: It just accelerated a few years.
sentences.zh: 它只是把这个进程加速了几年。

sentences.en: And we plan to continue to work with all of these organizations to make sure they can get the right information out to their users.
sentences.zh: 我们计划继续与所有这些组织合作，确保他们能够将正确的信息传达给用户。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I think we're good.
sentences.zh: 我想我们好了。

sentences.en: What Susan is saying, this change in YouTube, it's actually like a fundamental shift in the YouTube universe.
sentences.zh: 苏珊所说的YouTube的这种变化，实际上就像是YouTube宇宙中的一个根本性转变。

sentences.en: Like, for its entire existence, YouTube has been defined as an alternative media space.
sentences.zh: 就像在其存在的整个历史中，YouTube一直被定义为一个另类的媒体空间。

sentences.en: And the people that were there were like these insurgents and upstarts, these kind of like rebels and misfits.
sentences.zh: 在那里的人就像是这些叛乱分子和新贵，有点像反叛者和不合群的人。

sentences.en: And now YouTube is basically saying when it comes to certain things, we're going to let the establishment win.
sentences.zh: 而现在YouTube基本上是在说，当涉及到某些事情时，我们要让建制派获胜。

sentences.en: Which is tricky because the establishment isn't always right.
sentences.zh: 这很棘手，因为建制派并不总是对的。

sentences.en: Like, the World Health Organization has changed its guidance on things like face masks during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 比如，世界卫生组织在大流行期间改变了关于口罩等事情的指导方针。

sentences.en: So the ramifications of this change, they're not totally clear yet.
sentences.zh: 所以这种变化的后果目前还不是很清楚。

sentences.en: But what is clear is that this is going to be a huge battle.
sentences.zh: 但显而易见的是，这将是一场巨大的战斗。

sentences.en: Old school media does not like internet personalities because they're scared of us.
sentences.zh: 老派媒体不喜欢互联网名人，因为他们害怕我们。

sentences.en: We have so much influence and such a large void.
sentences.zh: 我们有这么大的影响力和如此巨大的空缺。

sentences.en: Because the internet culture that grew up on YouTube, not only has it gotten bigger than mainstream culture.
sentences.zh: 因为在YouTube上成长起来的互联网文化，不仅变得比主流文化更庞大。

sentences.en: Why is this an article?
sentences.zh: 为什么这是一篇文章？

sentences.en: Because clickbait.
sentences.zh: 因为标题党。

sentences.en: That's why.
sentences.zh: 这就是原因。

sentences.en: And not only does it distrust a lot of mainstream institutions.
sentences.zh: 而且它不仅不信任许多主流机构。

sentences.en: If there's anything I learned about the media from being a public figure is how they blatantly misrepresent people for their own personal gain.
sentences.zh: 如果说我作为一个公众人物对媒体有什么了解的话，那就是他们如何为了谋取私利而公然歪曲人们的事实。

sentences.en: But over time, it's basically come to despise them.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，它基本上开始鄙视他们。

sentences.en: I'm still here.
sentences.zh: 我还在这里。

sentences.en: I'm still making videos.
sentences.zh: 我还在制作视频。

sentences.zh: 干得好啊，《华尔街日报》。
